extracted.intended_audience: conference peer reviewers, area chairs, and researchers interested in peer review quality (machine learning / NeurIPS community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for reviewing and deciding on conference submissions, based on a NeurIPS 2014 experiment and a 2021 revisit analyzing reviewer consistency and review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjectivity is unavoidable — disclose reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjectivity is unavoidable — reviewers should disclose their reasoning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a large portion of reviewer score variation is subjective (the revisit finds ~50% subjective). To make decisions reproducible and interpretable, reviewers should explicitly state the subjective basis for their judgments and how personal taste or perspective influenced scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify scores explicitly with concrete criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify scores explicitly with concrete criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning numeric ratings, connect each score to concrete evaluation criteria (e.g., novelty, methodological soundness, clarity, significance). Avoid unexplained or one-line scores; provide concrete evidence or examples from the submission that motivate the rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'this is wrong' from 'I don't find it interesting'
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish "this is wrong" from "I don't find it interesting"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate objective correctness or technical flaws from subjective lack of interest or fit. In reviews, clearly label criticisms that are about correctness/validity versus those that are about perceived novelty or interest so area chairs can weigh them differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with author rebuttals to update on evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with author rebuttals to update on evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rebuttal period to reconsider initial judgments in light of authors' clarifications or fixes. Reviewers should update scores/comments when rebuttal evidence meaningfully addresses their concerns rather than leaving initial assessments unchanged by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge areas of uncertainty / state confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge their own areas of uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reviewer confidence or known limits of expertise. Explicitly indicate parts of the paper where the reviewer feels less qualified to judge, or where evidence is ambiguous, to help area chairs interpret disagreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat borderline papers with caution; do not over-trust narrow score margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Borderline papers are essentially random — area chairs should not over-trust narrow score margins
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For submissions near decision thresholds, recognize that committee agreement is low (2014 experiment showed ~25% inconsistent decisions for borderline papers and effectively coin-flip disagreement). Area chairs should rely more on discussion, broader evidence, or alternative acceptance models rather than tiny score differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize qualitative reviewer comments and discussion over raw scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion matters more than scores — qualitative reviewer comments contain more signal than ratings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize substantive written critiques and committee discussion when making accept/reject decisions. Scores are noisy; detailed comments, rationale, and dialogue often provide stronger signals about a paper's merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on filtering out poor work rather than reliably selecting the best
rubrics_metrics.description: The system filters out poor work but cannot reliably select the best
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer review primarily to identify clear weaknesses and filter low-quality submissions (rejected papers' scores correlated with later impact), but avoid treating acceptance as a reliable selector of future high-impact work (accepted papers' scores showed no correlation with citation impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider community attention / post-publication signals as complementary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Community attention is the real signal — citation counts reveal what reviews cannot predict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that pre-publication review is limited in forecasting long-term impact. Treat community response (citations, community uptake) as an important complementary measure and consider more inclusive acceptance policies or post-publication filtering mechanisms.
